node_definition.done_when:
Read the plan section with read_plan(view='section', section='s24') before starting; it is the authority. The FENCE — TIME line is composed in reckon/crew/prompts.py from the {time_budget} slot. The resume advice and its launch are composed in reckon/crew/dispatch.py. Take the launch instant from the attempt record the launch already writes, never from a second clock read that could disagree with it. Render the deadline as launch instant plus budget, in ISO-8601 UTC, together with the command date -u. In a new tests/test_a_time_fence_names_its_clock.py, render a dispatch prompt and a resume advice for a fixed launch instant and budget, with the clock injected, and assert that both carry the same deadline string. Execute the named negative control and confirm the parity assertion fails under it. The plan's report case is a manifest blocker citing an expired time fence before its deadline. Either land it inside this fence, or name in follow_ons the module that audits manifests and the case it needs. The gate is the new test plus every existing test file under tests/ that names compose_prompt, time_budget, FENCE or the resume advice, found by a text search. Run it at base and at head and list the files in the manifest. An evidence fragment at docs/evidence/fragments/crew-observability-truth/a-time-fence-names-its-clock.html records the change.
Run `date -u` first and treat that instant as your start; your deadline is 60 minutes later. Write your manifest before starting any long command. Run both gate arms with pytest-xdist (-n 8 --timeout=300), never serially. Start the base arm, from a `git archive` extraction of your base under /tmp in a directory named for this run, in the background, then run the head arm in the foreground, so they overlap. Each arm uses its own basetemp outside any repository and writes to its own new log path, which it never overwrites. Each arm is recorded as JSON carrying completed true and a literal command with absolute paths and no angle-bracket placeholder. Each log names its revision on the first line and ends with a bare line reading EXIT= followed by the exit code. The head arm adds no failure id; any added id means status blocked, naming each id. ruff check and ruff format --check over the changed Python paths report no finding the base did not. Scratch goes under /tmp in a directory named for this run and is deleted before status complete. The turn ends once the manifest reads complete or blocked.
